description: Seva is serving others without expecting anything in return. Gurbani teaches that through Seva, we lose our ego and find closeness to Waheguru.
Simran is the loving remembrance of Waheguru. By repeating His name with our heart and mind, we find peace and connect with the Divine.
Jot is the divine light of Waheguru that shines within everyone. Gurbani reminds us that the same light exists in every living being.
Jal means water, which cleanses our body. Gurbani compares the Name of Waheguru to cooling water that cleanses the mind of impurities.
Thal refers to the land or earth. Waheguru created both the water (Jal) and the land (Thal), and His presence is everywhere.
The Guru is the enlightener who takes us from darkness to light. Through the Guru's teachings (Gurbani), we learn how to live a truthful life.
The Mann (mind) can wander in many directions. Gurbani teaches us to control our mind and focus it on Waheguru to find true happiness.
Sangat is the company of holy people. Sitting in the Sangat helps us learn good virtues and inspires us to remember Waheguru.
Paap refers to bad deeds or actions that hurt others and distance us from Waheguru. Gurbani guides us to avoid Paap and perform Punn (good deeds).
Ninda is speaking ill of others. Gurbani strongly advises against Ninda, teaching us to look at our own faults instead of judging others.
Anand is a state of spiritual bliss and complete joy that comes from connecting with Waheguru. It is deeper and more lasting than worldly happiness.
